item.title: WFH Dads is crowdsourcing a holiday gift guide — and wants your picks
item.description:
Thom at WFH Dads is putting together a holiday gift guide for work-from-home dads, hoping to send it out early next week, and he's asking readers for help. He's looking for three kinds of suggestions: gifts for school-aged kids, gifts the whole family can enjoy, and gifts for dads to add to their own wish lists — or just treat themselves with.

If you've gotten something that fits, he's inviting readers to reply with it, and he may include it in the guide. It's a small, community-sourced ask — but if you're a WFH dad still hunting for gift ideas, the finished guide next week should be worth a look.

Sources

  • WFH Dads: Could use your help with something…

item.title: Time blocking for work-from-home dads that actually works
item.description:
A new piece from WFH Dads takes on time blocking for fathers working from home — and argues the trick isn't a rigid schedule but a baseline you adjust as the week changes. Instead of a fixed grid that falls apart the first time a kid gets sick or a meeting moves, the approach starts with a default week and flexes around real life.

The idea comes out of the author's Workday Reset program, and the pitch is aimed at dads juggling deep work, school runs, and household chaos in the same four walls: a system that survives contact with an actual week, rather than one that only works on paper.

Sources
